I fixed the handshake failure by having debug builds trust the dev CA. I could not build or run the app here, so this is verified by reading the files only.

**Cause:** The debug build calls `https://10.0.2.2:8443/` (`app/build.gradle.kts:19`). That server uses the self-signed certificate in `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`, which Android doesn't trust by default, so the TLS handshake fails.

**Changes (all new files, debug source set only):**
- `app/src/debug/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem`: a copy of the dev CA certificate, so the app can load it. I copied the contents by hand, so check it matches `dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem` if the error persists.
- `app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`: trusts that CA (plus system CAs) for the host `10.0.2.2` only.
- `app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`: attaches that config to the application.

**Choices I made:**
- I scoped the trust to the debug build and to the single host `10.0.2.2`, so release builds (`api.shelftap.example`, public certificate) are unchanged.
- I did not disable certificate validation in `CatalogClient.kt`. That would have been the simpler fix, but it would weaken TLS checks for every host.

To confirm, rebuild the debug variant and run `CatalogClient.fetchCatalog()` against the running dev server in the emulator. The dev server must be up (`docker compose up` in the server repo) for the request to succeed.
